gaps_acknowledged: No Databricks experience (posting names Databricks workflows and cloud platforms)
No dedicated time-series forecasting work (ARIMA, SARIMA, Prophet, exponential smoothing, LSTM, TFT) and no forecast-accuracy metrics such as MAE, RMSE or MAPE
No production-deployed or shipped anomaly-detection model; closest evidence is data-quality validation work
No industrial or manufacturing domain experience
No Sales, Finance or controlling domain exposure beyond market-sizing and revenue forecasting at Ipsos Strategy3
No ERP (SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365) or formal scrum agile experience
key_tailoring_decisions: Added Ipsos Strategy3 as a third work entry so the market-sizing and revenue-forecasting evidence answers the posting's forecasting and predictive-modelling requirement directly, and reframed the UK Biobank dissertation as a predictive-modelling project (logistic regression vs XGBoost, LightGBM, random forests, calibration and decision curves, feature/threshold/scoring-logic testing) rather than a causal one

Framed the anomaly-detection requirement honestly as data-quality work (export defects found, deprecated tags rebuilt to reproduce a ~60M-user segment at DS Digital Technology) and stated plainly in the letter that no production anomaly-detection model has been shipped, instead of implying a modelling technique she has not used

Opened the company paragraph on independently verified Atlas Copco facts (decentralised organisation since 1873, UK business present since 1919 with the Hemel Hempstead head office) and tied decentralisation to why a group reporting platform must earn trust across entities; the Mandarin and China work is named once in the DS Digital paragraph rather than bolted onto the visa sentence
warnings: The posting's Preferred Time Series Requirement (forecasting models on time-dependent data, and MAE/RMSE/MAPE forecast-accuracy metrics) is a genuine gap. It is acknowledged in the cover letter rather than papered over, and it is the most likely screening risk for this application.
No Databricks experience, which the posting names as the CODA platform. Also acknowledged in the letter.
The posting names Talent Acquisition contact April Harbour but states no application deadline, so the deadline field is empty rather than guessed.
